assumptions: D73 (decided-by: pending, the lead assigned the id but it is not in DECISIONS.md yet): realtime postgres_changes delivery relies on the existing SELECT policies (payments_select, gateway_bills_select) being applied to the subscriber's JWT. Tenants therefore only get rows for their own leases and staff only get rows for their own org, so no new grants or policies were added.

gateway_bills rows are updated when their status changes. The tables keep the default replica identity (primary key), so UPDATE events carry the full new row but only the primary key of the old row. I did not set REPLICA IDENTITY FULL, because that would publish old row contents and is not needed for a status refresh in the portal.

The migration is not idempotent: re-adding a table that is already in the publication fails. That is fine for the normal flow, a db reset from zero followed by migrations applied in order, because the supabase_realtime publication starts empty on local Supabase.
Only payments and gateway_bills are published, as the brief specified. Invoices are not published, so the portal has to refetch invoice balances when a payment or gateway-bill event arrives.

ui.status: Done. The tenant portal now subscribes to Realtime changes on payments and gateway_bills after the first successful load. tsc and eslint on src/components/tenant are clean. I did not run the 1192 existing tests or the portal in a browser.
assumptions: The channel 'tenant-portal' listens to '*' events on public.payments and public.gateway_bills. I added no lease_id filter, because RLS already limits events to the tenant's own leases.

Events are debounced by 300 ms into one refetch. Each burst shows one toast, 'Payment status updated', and then bumps reloadKey. That refetch does not clear data, so the skeleton does not flash. The toast shows when the debounce fires, not on each raw event.

The subscription effect depends on a loadedOnce flag that stays true after the first successful load. The manual Refresh button, which sets data to null, therefore does not tear down and re-create the channel.
Cleanup clears the pending timer and calls supabase.removeChannel(channel).

I did not change the migration. 20261026000004_realtime.sql already adds both tables to the supabase_realtime publication. If db reset has not been run since that migration was added, no events will arrive until it is.
I did not test live delivery. Whether the Realtime server honours the RLS policies for the tenant's JWT depends on the running stack.

tests.status:
done. I added /home/electronica-care/ezy-prep/exam/app/tests/rls/realtime.test.ts with describe 'R42 R56 realtime respects RLS'. I ran it twice in a row with `bash ../scripts/with-db.sh npx vitest run tests/rls/realtime.test.ts` and both runs passed: "Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 1 passed (1)", about 15.8 s each. `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint tests/rls/realtime.test.ts --max-warnings=0` are clean. The publication check printed 1 on the first try, so I did not need to poll.

What the test does: tenant A (on the lease), tenant B (same org, with their own lease on another unit) and the manager of a second fixture org each subscribe to INSERT events on public.payments. Each uses userClient(token) and then await realtime.setAuth(token), because userClient only sets the REST Authorization header. The fixture manager then records a cash payment of 100 sen on tenant A's lease through POST /api/leases/<id>/payments. The test asserts the response is 201, tenant A receives an INSERT with that payment id within 15 s, and tenant B and the other org's manager receive no events at all over the whole 15 s window. afterAll removes every channel, disconnects realtime and closes the pool.

Realtime does deliver to tenant A, so there is no environment problem. My first run did fail: tenant A got nothing. A temporary debug test (deleted afterwards) showed the cause. The 'SUBSCRIBED' status only means the channel joined. The postgres_changes stream goes live about 1 s later, when the server sends the system message {extension:'postgres_changes', status:'ok', message:'Subscribed to PostgreSQL'}. So the subscribe helper now waits for both signals, within the same 20 s timeout. If that system message arrives with an error status, the test fails straight away with the server's message. This is a correctness fix, not a weaker test: waiting only for 'SUBSCRIBED' lets the INSERT happen before the stream is live, which gives a false 'tenant A got nothing'.

Matrix covered: on the payments INSERT realtime channel, the lease's tenant receives the event; a same-org tenant on a different lease receives nothing; another org's manager receives nothing. Gaps: same-org manager and staff receiving the event, anon subscribers, gateway_bills (also in the publication per D73), and UPDATE events (for example approve or void) are not covered. I found no contract gap.

bash ../scripts/with-db.sh npx vitest run tests/rls/realtime.test.ts (second run in a row) -> Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 1 passed (1), 15.76s
assumptions: A subscription counts as ready only when 'SUBSCRIBED' has fired AND the postgres_changes system message with status 'ok' has arrived; waiting on SUBSCRIBED alone gave a false failure.

Tenant B was given their own lease on F.unitIds[1] (inserted with insertLease), so they can legitimately SELECT payments. A missing per-row RLS filter would then leak tenant A's event to them, whereas a tenant with no lease could pass by accident.
Added a third negative subscriber (another fixture org's manager) to cover cross-org realtime isolation; this goes beyond the brief's two subscribers.

The negative subscribers must receive zero events of any kind during the window, not just none for this payment id. Nothing else writes payments visible to them, so this stricter check is safe even with other test files running in parallel.
The 15 s window is measured from just before the POST. Tenant B and the other manager are checked only after the full window has passed, even when tenant A's event arrives earlier.
The DATABASE_URL from .env.local is passed to psql explicitly; a bare psql under with-db.sh tries the local socket as the OS user and fails.
